talk_track: I ran platform engineering at Ripple through 6B+ annual transactions, and PayPal's internal developer platform for 9,000 engineers before that, so I've watched what happens when corridors grow faster than the engineering underneath them. Your Product Manager, Onboarding posting puts it plainly: "We have built a world-class financial engine. Now we need an onboarding experience that matches it." Read alongside the Developer Experience Lead req — "how external developers experience that engine has no owner" — those two openings are describing one number rather than two: how many OpenFX people it takes to get one institution live and trading. At $45B annualized across 100+ institutional clients, that number decides whether each new corridor compounds margin or just adds a delivery team. In my experience that is almost always solved with plumbing — a self-serve integration path, API governance, docs that stay true as the platform moves — and only rarely with more headcount. What does it cost you today to get one institution to first trade?
